content:
The answer is **A. integrated**.

Integrated project delivery is concerned with all aspects of building performance and requires coordination of different building systems to avoid rework. This approach brings together all stakeholders (architects, engineers, contractors, etc.) early in the project to collaborate and coordinate their efforts throughout the entire project lifecycle.

Key characteristics of integrated project delivery include:
- Early involvement of all team members
- Shared risk and reward
- Collaborative decision-making
- Focus on optimizing the entire project rather than individual phases
- Enhanced coordination to prevent conflicts and rework between building systems

Sequential delivery (option C) involves completing one phase before starting the next, which can lead to more rework when coordination issues arise later. "Noncompound" (option B) is not a standard term used in project delivery methods.
